title: Estás ilusionada, ¿verdad?
goal: a usar las coletillas isn't it?, don't you?… y a darles la entonación correcta

ex.t: You're excited about the trip, aren't you?
I always get nervous before a flight.
ex.es: Siempre me pongo nerviosa antes de un vuelo.

ex.t: She was upset because nobody called her.
ex.es: Estaba disgustada porque nadie la llamó.

ex.t: I was so relieved when the doctor phoned.
ex.es: Me quedé tan aliviada cuando llamó el médico.

ex.t: We were disappointed with the hotel.
I'm a bit jealous of your holiday!
ex.es: ¡Te tengo un poco de envidia por tus vacaciones!

ex.t: My aunt feels lonely since she retired.
ex.es: Mi tía se siente sola desde que se jubiló.

vocab.note: Alone = sola (sin nadie). Lonely = que se siente sola.

ex.t: I was very moved by his speech.

pron.title: La coletilla que baja y la que sube
pron.tip: Si la voz BAJA al final (↘), solo confirmas lo que ya sabes: It's lovely, isn't it? ↘. Si SUBE (↗), preguntas de verdad porque dudas: You've got the tickets, haven't you? ↗

exercises.q: Your aunt lives on her own, ___?
exercises.why: Lives sin auxiliar, con she: doesn't she?

exercises.q: You were very moved at the wedding, ___?
You get nervous on planes, ___ you?
exercises.es: Te pones nerviosa en los aviones, ¿verdad?
exercises.why: Get sin auxiliar, con you: don't you?

exercises.q: They haven't been to San Francisco, ___ they?
exercises.es: No han estado en San Francisco, ¿verdad?

exercises.q: You were relieved when he called, ___ you?
Your grandson is very excited, isn't it?
exercises.why: Hablamos de tu nieto: isn't he?

exercises.q: You feel a bit lonely, isn't you?
exercises.why: Feel no lleva be: don't you?

exercises.q: You were disappointed with the hotel.
answer: You were disappointed with the hotel, weren't you?

exercises.context: Hace un sol precioso en San Francisco. Quieres empezar una charla con la señora de al lado.
options: It's a beautiful day, isn't it? ↘
It's a beautiful day, doesn't it? ↘
It's a beautiful day, is it? ↗
exercises.answer: It's a beautiful day, isn't it? ↘
exercises.why: Afirmativa con is → isn't it?, con la voz bajando: solo das conversación.

exercises.context: No estás segura de si tu marido ha cogido los billetes y se lo preguntas de verdad.
options: You've got the tickets, haven't you? ↗
You've got the tickets, haven't you? ↘
You've got the tickets, don't you? ↗
exercises.answer: You've got the tickets, haven't you? ↗
exercises.why: Dudas de verdad: la voz sube. Y con have got, haven't you?

exercises.t: It's a beautiful view, isn't it?

dialog.title: Mirando el Golden Gate
dialog.setting: Yolanda charla con una señora en un mirador frente al Golden Gate

lines.t: It's a wonderful view, isn't it?
It's beautiful. The bridge isn't really red, is it?
lines.es: Es preciosa. El puente no es rojo de verdad, ¿no?

lines.t: No, the colour is called International Orange.
lines.es: No, el color se llama International Orange.

lines.t: How funny! You live here, don't you?
Yes, but my daughter lives in Spain. I miss her.
lines.es: Sí, pero mi hija vive en España. La echo de menos.

lines.t: Oh, you feel a bit lonely, don't you?
lines.es: Ay, se siente un poco sola, ¿verdad?

lines.t: Sometimes. But I'm visiting her in May. I'm so excited!
lines.es: A veces. Pero voy a verla en mayo. ¡Estoy ilusionadísima!

lines.t: You'll love it. Spain is lovely in May!
lines.es: Le va a encantar. ¡España está preciosa en mayo!

questions.q: ¿Cómo se llama el color del puente?
¿Cuándo va a ver Margaret a su hija?

realLife.context: Para empezar una charla con alguien desconocido, muy a la inglesa

summary: Afirmativa → coletilla negativa: It's lovely, isn't it?
Negativa → coletilla afirmativa: She isn't upset, is she?
Sin auxiliar: do / does / did (You live here, don't you?)
Voz que baja ↘ = confirmo; voz que sube ↗ = pregunto de verdad
Emociones: excited, nervous, upset, relieved, lonely, moved
